text:
Jordan: Hi @Sam / @Ava — quick heads up, I'm requesting an accommodation for the upcoming performance check-in. I get really anxious in live 1:1 review meetings and prefer written feedback or an asynchronous option.
Sam: Thanks for flagging this, Jordan. Can you share a bit about what format would work best? Written only, or a short agenda sent ahead, or audio notes?
Jordan: Written-only is ideal. Video/phone calls spike my anxiety. I can do a short written self-review + written Qs for you to answer.
Sam: I want to make sure we keep the review fair across the team. Is this a permanent need or temporary?
Jordan: It's been ongoing. I think an ongoing accommodation makes sense. Happy to provide whatever documentation is needed.
Ava (People Ops): @Jordan thanks for telling us — we can absolutely explore reasonable accommodations here. Options we've supported before: written review exchange, pre-submitted questions, recorded responses with captions, or a neutral third-party scribe in a shorter live meeting. All are ADA-compatible depending on role duties.
Ava (People Ops): @Sam — from a manager perspective we usually accept written alternatives as long as the evaluation criteria and rubric stay the same. We can help draft an agreement.
Sam: Ok, that sounds workable. I just want to avoid inadvertently weakening the feedback loop. If we do written, can we agree on a timeline?
Jordan: Timeline works for me — draft self-review by Friday, manager response within one week.
Ava (People Ops): I'll put together a simple accommodation memo template and next steps. @peopleops-bot can also send the formal request link so Jordan can attach any clinician note if they choose.
peopleops-bot: <https://redwood.internal/hr/accom-request|Submit accommodation request> — Use this to start the formal accommodation process.
Dan (HR Lead): Quick note from HR: document the agreed alternative in writing (manager + employee + People Ops). This protects confidentiality and ensures consistent process. We can also offer manager coaching on giving written feedback that maps to our competency rubric.
Sam: Thanks @Dan — that coaching would help me frame written feedback better.
Jordan: Appreciate it. One more thing — on-call rotation: live handing off during incidents is stressful. Would it be possible to swap on-call weeks or pair me with someone who handles the live call-in and I do async follow-up?
Ava (People Ops): That's a reasonable ask. We'll work with Eng leads to adjust schedules where feasible. Please mark that preference in the formal request form so we can track operational impacts.
Sam: I can arrange a buddy for live incident responses for the next quarter and we'll re-evaluate.
Jordan: Thank you all. Really helps to know there's a path. :relieved:
Ava (People Ops): I'll DM you both to draft the memo. We'll aim to have the accommodation agreement and coaching scheduled within two weeks.
peopleops-bot: Note: accommodation requests are confidential and only shared with necessary stakeholders.
Sam: Sounds good. Jordan — I'll block time to write my feedback when I get your self-review.
Jordan: Sending the self-review tonight. Appreciate everyone moving quickly. :heart:
